projectDir.description: Directory holding the project, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.

version-declared.name: Node.js version is declared
version-declared.description: The project declares the Node.js version it is built and run against, and that version is no older than the configured floor.
version-declared.remediation: Declare the runtime where the project already describes itself: `"engines": { "node": ">=20" }` in `package.json`, or an `.nvmrc` file naming the exact release. Without one, the runtime is whatever the runner happens to have, so a syntax or standard library difference shows up in CI instead of on the laptop where it was introduced.

minVersion.description: Oldest Node.js version accepted. A declared version below this is a violation.

lockfile-committed.name: Node.js dependencies are locked
lockfile-committed.description: The project commits a lock file, so an install of the same commit resolves the same versions.
lockfile-committed.remediation:
Commit the lock file your package manager writes:

```bash
npm install      # writes package-lock.json
pnpm install     # writes pnpm-lock.yaml
yarn install     # writes yarn.lock
```

A `^` or `~` range resolves to whatever the registry serves that day, so without a lock file the build that shipped is not the build that was reviewed.

single-package-manager.name: One package manager owns the tree
single-package-manager.description: The project commits at most one lock file, so two package managers don't both try to manage the dependency tree.
single-package-manager.remediation: Pick the package manager the project actually uses and delete the other lock files. A checkout with both `package-lock.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` installs different versions depending on which command the developer or CI step runs. The lock file nobody uses drifts silently until someone does use it.

package-manager-pinned.name: Package manager is pinned
package-manager-pinned.description: The manifest names the package manager and the exact version Corepack should install.
package-manager-pinned.remediation:
Name the package manager and its version in `package.json`. This is the version Corepack installs:

```json
{
  "packageManager": "pnpm@9.1.0"
}
```

Without this field, or with a name but no version, the install runs under whichever npm, pnpm or yarn the runner happens to have. A lock file written by one package manager is then resolved by another, and the tree a developer reviewed is not the tree CI installs.
